periods.analysis: Prevention lessons reached 1,650 students using interim materials while the district reviews the new curriculum, and after-school programs served 190 teens. Discipline alternatives have not started at any campus and the policy audit is waiting on documents, so the goal starts at Caution.
periods.recommendations: Complete the curriculum review, present a restorative-response draft to district student services, and chase outstanding policies.

periods.analysis: Lessons reached 2,100 students and teen programs 245, and the family prevention guide is finished. The district deferred discipline changes until the new school year, and the curriculum review ended in June with revisions requested, so we are holding this goal at Caution until teachers are trained.
periods.recommendations: Finalize the curriculum and train teachers before school opens, and take the restorative-response model to district leaders.

periods.analysis: Classroom prevention lessons and after-school programs are both on pace to finish the year as planned, and prevention materials are now in the hands of families at every middle school. The school discipline alternatives strategy is the one lagging piece, because only a few campuses have adopted the new response model. Policy review work will inform whether this needs a formal district action.
periods.recommendations: Secure a district liaison for discipline alternatives and finish the policy audit.
